subject: MerchantX production impact after v2.7 quant rollout
messages:
From: Alex Tan <alex.tan@merchantx.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production degradation after model upgrade

Jasmine,

We pushed your v2.7 quant profile last night (q6) and since ~08:45 PT we're seeing a widespread checkout slowdown and a spike in downstream errors. Key metrics: p95 latency jumped from ~210ms to ~890ms, 4xx/5xx error rate climbed to 4.2% (was <0.2%), and sustained throughput fell ~30% under normal load. This is impacting customer checkouts across US-West and causing a backlog in our ingestion workers.

Attached: short perf screenshot + request logs. We're reverting on our side isn't possible since the model is only available via your hosted endpoint. Please advise immediate mitigation. This is a Sev2 for us.

- Alex
Alex Tan | Head of Platform Engineering
MerchantX
attachments: perf_screenshot.png, merchantx_requestlog_20270620.txt

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production degradation after model upgrade (MerchantX)

Thanks for flagging — initial read: the v2.7 deployment included a quantization profile shift (q4 -> q6) and a default per-request batch size bump in the runtime optimization for that model family. My immediate hypotheses:

1) Kernel selection mismatch on a subset of older GPU nodes (some nodes served the new kernels compiled for q6 but are falling back to less-optimized paths under heavy concurrency, amplifying latency).
2) KV-cache alignment/regeneration overhead with the new profile causing repeated cache misses for hot prefixes (explains throughput collapse).
3) Edge path differences for MerchantX route (regional routing pushed more traffic to us-west-2 where we have a higher ratio of mixed-generation hardware).

Plan in next 45m:
- Grab perf traces + stack dumps from affected routes (Infra).
- Rollback option: pin model variant to v2.6 (non-q6 profile) as a hotfix; this is fastest and compatible.
- If rollback is risky, we can also enable a runtime compatibility shim to force slower but stable kernel paths while we repro locally.

Stephanie, can your team attempt the v2.6 pin canary (10% in us-west-2) and monitor p95 and error rate? I'll coordinate logs and share a short RCA once we confirm root cause.

-Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production degradation after model upgrade (MerchantX)

Action plan and timelines (operational):

1) Canaries: starting now, we will pin MerchantX route to v2.6 for a 10% canary in us-west-2. Expected telemetry within 5-10 minutes.
2) If canary p95 drops to baseline and error rate <0.5%, we will expand canary to 50% and then full region. Estimated mitigation to <15 minutes once canary is healthy.
3) Rollback steps documented here: https://app.redwood.com/rollouts/rollout-6382 (internal runbook).
4) Communication: Jasmine, please send the one-line rollback notice to MerchantX and CS; Monica please prepare suggested credits for their SLA exposure and set up a postmortem meeting with them for tomorrow.

I'm kicking off the rollout now. I'll upload perf_report_v2p7.pdf and the runtime logs to the incident folder once collected.

-Stephanie
SRE Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: perf_report_v2p7.pdf, capture_logs_2027-06-20.tar.gz

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Alex Tan <alex.tan@merchantx.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation after model upgrade

Alex — we're sorry for the outage. We have initiated a targeted mitigation: pinning your route to v2.6 (non-q6 profile) as a canary in us-west-2. Stephanie's team has started telemetry checks; we expect visible improvements within 10 minutes and full regional rollback in ~30 minutes if the canary is healthy.

We will follow up with a short postmortem and a timeline for a safe re-roll of v2.7 once we've resolved kernel compatibility and KV-cache regressions. Monica will reach out about SLA credits; we're prioritizing MerchantX steadily.

Please share any additional request traces you can — they help correlate user prefixes. I'm on call today and available for a bridge.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
